claim: Mammalian PHB2 is an inner-membrane mitophagy receptor binding LC3 via a LIR
finding: PHB2 binds LC3 through a LIR upon depolarisation and proteasome-dependent outer membrane rupture; LIR mutation blocks mitophagy; phb-2 RNAi blocks paternal mitochondria clearance in C. elegans
context: HeLa/MEF cells; C. elegans tested only by clearance phenotype
confidence: high for mammals; the worm arm is a phenotype, not a binding assay

finding: Region 121-124 annotated 'LC3-interaction region'; residues read Y121-Q122-R123-L124 (YQRL); mouse O35129 identical
confidence: database-level; position is consistent with the primary paper

claim: Worm PHB-2 retains the mammalian LIR core
finding: P50093 vs Q99623: 62.9% identity over 294 columns, gapless at the window, uniform -1 offset. Human 117-128 LPSMYQRLGLDY aligns to worm 116-127 LVHIYRTLGQNW. X0 Y121->Y120 retained, X1 Q122->R121 substituted, X2 R123->T122 substituted, X3 L124->L123 retained. No D/E at -1 to -4 in either
confidence: alignment is unambiguous; functional meaning is not established

claim: Topology permits or forbids a direct LIR interaction
finding: TM 20-42 annotated 'Helical; Signal-anchor for type II membrane protein'; Kyte-Doolittle window-19 peak at worm residue 28 (1.77). Motif at 120-123 sits 78 residues C-terminal to the anchor, so it faces the intermembrane space. Only residues 1-19 are in the matrix
context: C. elegans sequence; topology is an annotation plus prediction, no worm protease-protection data found
confidence: medium; direction of the anchor is inferred from the type II assignment

claim: The LIR is available for ATG8 docking in the resting complex
finding: Across 16 PHB2 chains and 54 chain-residue pairs, Y121 and L124 lose 41-94% of accessibility when placed in the assembly (Wilcoxon W=0, p=1.6e-10, median drop 10.4 pp). The burying partner is a PHB1 chain in all three structures
context: human PHB1/PHB2 cryo-EM assemblies at 2.4, 3.1 and 2.8 A; no worm structure exists
confidence: high for human; transfer to worm rests on 62.9% identity and the shared PHB/SPFH ring

claim: Core retention predicts a functional LIR
finding: Human PHB1 (P35232) has F107-T-S-I110 and worm PHB-1 (Q9BKU4) has Y110-L-N-I113 at the equivalent fold position, both satisfying [WFY]xx[LIV]. AlphaFold monomer RSA is near-identical across all four (X0 18-24%, X3 8-14%). Worm PHB-2 carries 6 such cores overall
confidence: high; PHB1 is reported not to bind LC3 directly, so the core alone is not sufficient

citation: this work (NW alignment of ATG8 family)
claim: Which worm ATG8 the motif could engage
finding: LGG-1 is GABARAP-type (82.9% to GABARAP), LGG-2 is LC3-type (56.7% to LC3B). LGG-2 keeps the LC3B docking site at HP2 7/8 and rim 6/8 identical; LGG-1 has L22K, L63F, S115D. Rim net charge LGG-2 +5.0, LGG-1 +1.0. The worm X1 Arg sits over that basic rim
context: sequence and alignment only, no binding measurement
confidence: medium; electrostatic reasoning is compositional, not an energy calculation

claim: Which ATG8 acts on sperm-derived organelles
finding: Both LGG-1 and LGG-2 are recruited to sperm-derived organelles, with distinct roles in degradation versus transport
confidence: high for recruitment; does not address PHB-2 binding

claim: Worm phb-2 interacts with lgg-1 and lgg-2
finding: lgg-1 0.982 and lgg-2 0.973 combined score, but database channel exactly 0.900 for both (pathway co-membership), textmining 0.698/0.567, coexpression 0.094/0.049. Compare phb-2 to phb-1: coexpression 0.946, experiments 0.969
confidence: high that this is not independent worm evidence

claim: PHB-2 acts at mitochondria in C. elegans
finding: The worm prohibitin-2 ortholog is reported outside mitochondria, associating with the MEC-2 mechanosensory complex
confidence: medium; a non-mitochondrial pool complicates a CC assignment

claim: Prohibitin phenotypes in the worm run through mitophagy
finding: Prohibitin-depletion longevity requires autophagy but not mitophagy
confidence: medium; separates the autophagy requirement from mitophagy
